note: 'The maximum inner diameter of this enclosure is about 14 m', p. 347. Rounded by the authors; the enclosure is oval. Checked against the publisher's PDF by the night builder, 20 October 2026.
'Its peripheral wall, preserved to an elevation of over 3 m', p. 347: a lower bound. Checked against the publisher's PDF by the night builder, 20 October 2026.
'connects (so far) 11 T-shaped pillars', p. 347: as excavated by 2019, not a count of the original ring. Checked against the publisher's PDF by the night builder, 20 October 2026.
'Its central pillars ... the twin central pillars', p. 347. Checked against the publisher's PDF by the night builder, 20 October 2026.

'Its central pillars with anthropomorphic depictions, rising to a height of 5.5 m, are the largest megalithic features on the site', p. 347; p. 344 says 'up to 5.5 m high'. One figure for the pair. Checked against the publisher's PDF by the night builder, 20 October 2026.
'shallow pedestals or platform-like bases (20–30 cm high) carved out of the bedrock forming the enclosure floor', p. 347. Checked against the publisher's PDF by the night builder, 20 October 2026.
